source_title: Uttarakhand targets developed state status by 2047, CM Pushkar Dhami unveils rs 7,844-crore supplementary - The Times of India
source_excerpt: DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Tuesday said the state government was committed to transforming Uttarakhand into a developed, prosperous and self-reliant state by 2047. He said the government was accelerating development activities and ensuring that the benefits of welfare schemes reached the last person in society.Addressing a press conference at Gairsain (Bhararisain), Dhami said the supplementary budget for the financial year 2026â27 had been prepared keeping in mind both the state's immediate requirements and its long-term development goals.The chief minister said Uttarakhand had made significant progress in nearly 26 years since its formation, crediting the achievements to the sacrifices of statehood movement activists, the hard work of the people and public participation. He added that the state was committed to contributing to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of a developed India by 2047.Highlighting the state's economic progress, Dhami said Uttarakhand's Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) had increased from approximately Rs 2.55 lakh crore in 2022 to a projected Rs 3.82 lakh crore in 2026â27. Per capita income had also risen from around Rs 1.95 lakh to Rs 2.74 lakh during the period.He said multidimensional poverty had declined, while the number of startups had grown from 702 to 1,978 and the number of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) had increased from approximately 60,000 to one lakh. The state had also recorded significant growth in solar energy capacity.Dhami said Uttarakhand had secured joint first place nationally, with a score of 79, in NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023â24. The state had also received national recognition for its investment-friendly environment and financial management. He said the government was focused on ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reached villages, farmers, women and young people.Rs 7,844-crore supplementary budgetThe chief minister said the supplementary budget for 2026â27 proposed an allocation of Rs 7,844.18 crore, comprising Rs 4,164.32 crore for capital expenditure and Rs 3,679.86 crore for revenue expenditure.In line with the recommendations of the Sixth State Finance Commission, the government has proposed increasing the share of local bodies in the state's tax revenue from 10.5% to 12.5%. An allocation of Rs 721 crore has been made for this purpose to provide additional resources to rural and urban local bodies for development works.Dhami said Rs 1,100 crore had been allocated under the Annapurti Scheme for procuring paddy and wheat from farmers, Rs 500 crore under the Special Assistance Scheme for infrastructure development and Rs 300 crore for the Jal Jeevan Mission.The budget also provides Rs 122 crore for the Gairsain Water Supply Dam Project and approximately Rs 290 crore for preparations and infrastructure facilities for the upcoming Divya Kumbh. Provisions have also been made for works related to the Nanda Raj Jat Yatra and the Haridwar-Ganga Corridor.Healthcare, education and youth welfare in focusThe chief minister said Rs 100 crore had been allocated for the Atal Ayushman Scheme to expand healthcare services, while Rs 125 crore had been earmarked for the Golden Card Scheme for government employees.Approximately Rs 160 crore has been provided for medical education-related works, including those at the medical colleges in Pithoragarh and Rudrapur. Another Rs 200 crore has been allocated for digital learning in school and higher education.He said the budget also included provisions for the Mukhyamantri Yuva Bhavishya Nirman Yojana, a sports university, a women's sports college, athlete training programmes and scholarships for young people preparing for competitive examinations.Women and child welfare, the Poshan Abhiyaan, honorariums for midday meal cooks, farmers' pensions and other social security schemes have also been accorded priority, he added.Dhami said the government's focus extended beyond launching schemes to ensuring their timely implementation and delivery of benefits. Public participation had been encouraged in the budget-making process, with pre-budget consultations held over the past five years to gather suggestions from farmers, women, young people, entrepreneurs and representatives of various sectors.He said the government had maintained a revenue-surplus position while emphasising fiscal discipline, transparency and the efficient utilisation of public funds.Disaster resilience and IT sector developmentDhami said the government was giving priority to disaster management and the development of safe infrastructure, particularly in vulnerable areas. Work was underway in land subsidence-affected areas, including Joshimath, alongside efforts to promote disaster-resilient construction and improve basic infrastructure for road and helicopter services.He also said a Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) facility had been established in Dehradun for the first time, creating new opportunities for young people in the information technology and startup sectors.The chief minister said the government aimed to preserve Uttarakhand's heritage and culture while pursuing economic growth. With the goal of building a prosperous state by 2035, the government was focusing on quality investment, local employment, improved public services and the expansion of modern facilities.Dhami said Uttarakhand's progress was the result of collective efforts and that the government's objective was to ensure that development schemes benefited every citizen.
